body_text:
An ideal $I$ of a commutative ring $R$ is an additive subgroup
such that $ri\in I$ for every $r\in R$ and $i\in I$. Ideals,
rather than arbitrary subrings, are precisely the subsets for
which coset multiplication is well defined. The quotient $R/I$
is a ring under $(r+I)+(s+I)=(r+s)+I$ and $(r+I)(s+I)=rs+I$.
